tema: Cleft Sentences — It was... who/that & What... was

cast_dialogue.linea: Sometimes a sentence needs a spotlight, heroes. Cleft sentences split the message to shine a light exactly where you want it.
It was Kenji who organized the surprise party, not me. What I contributed was my old photo projector.
It was Sofía who chose the music. What Abuela Carmen prepared was a mountain of tamales!
It wasn't the gifts that moved everyone — it was the speech that the old man gave at midnight.
What I remember now is the silence before the toast. It was that silence that said everything, mis héroes.

inicio.definicion_pragmatica: Cleft sentences create emphasis by splitting one idea in two: 'It + be + FOCUS + who/that...' (It was Kenji who...) or 'What-clause + be + FOCUS' (What we need is time). Use them to correct, contrast or highlight: 'It wasn't the gifts — it was the speech.'

guion: Sofía: The surprise party was perfect. Was it you who organized it, Ben?
Ben: No — it was Kenji who organized everything. I only brought my old projector.
Ben: It was me who chose it, actually. Do you liked it?
Sofía: I loved it! But it wasn't the gifts that moved me...
Sofía: It was the speech that the old man gave at midnight.
Ben: You're right. What I'll always remember is the silence before the toast.

reading.texto: It was Kenji who organized the surprise party, but it was Sofía who chose the music. What Ben contributed was his old photo projector, and what Abuela Carmen prepared was a mountain of tamales. It wasn't the gifts that moved everyone — it was the speech that the old man gave at midnight. What we all remember now is the silence before the toast, and it was that silence that said everything.

preguntas.afirmacion: The gifts moved everyone the most.
